title: Docker: reproducible images, non-root runtime and Compose
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects docker: reproducible images, non-root runtime and compose with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Deployment evidence includes the image build, API smoke tests and persistent-index restart test when that backend is enabled.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An image packages filesystem layers and runtime metadata; a container is an isolated running instance. Dockerfile layer order affects dependency cache reuse. Copying dependency manifests before application source lets source-only changes avoid reinstalling dependencies.

Containers improve reproducibility but do not automatically provide secure isolation, persistent data or correct service discovery. Secrets baked into layers can remain recoverable even if deleted later.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use a pinned base image policy, locked dependencies, a non-root user and a narrow build context. Set an explicit working directory, install dependencies before copying source and launch uvicorn on the container interface. Provide health/readiness endpoints and graceful shutdown.

Compose connects the API and optional Qdrant on an internal network with named persistent volumes. Keep provider secrets in runtime environment or secret mounts; exclude .env, caches and credentials with .dockerignore. Multi-stage builds can remove compilers from the final runtime.
sections.code:
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
USER 10001
CMD ["uvicorn","app:app","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","8000"]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: The service listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container and is unreachable through a published port. A vector collection disappears after restart because no volume was attached. An image contains a copied .env.
Test build context, non-root identity, port reachability, health checks, volume persistence and stop behavior. Scan the image and verify dependency versions against the lockfile.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Deployment evidence includes the image build, API smoke tests and persistent-index restart test when that backend is enabled. Document fixture-only and live-provider modes explicitly.
For an SDET, container tests are environment contract tests: the same synthetic request must behave consistently in the virtual environment and container, with configuration supplied externally.

takeaway: Deployment evidence includes the image build, API smoke tests and persistent-index restart test when that backend is enabled.

title: Container smoke tests: data paths, ports and persistence
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects container smoke tests: data paths, ports and persistence with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance evidence includes image identity, non-root identity, endpoint results, dataset path and restart behavior.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A local import working in a virtual environment does not prove the container image works. Working directories, module paths, user permissions and dataset locations can differ. The shared service uses a configured dataset root so its domain code does not depend on the checkout's parent directory layout.
Build context determines which files are available to COPY. The repository-root context includes local-labs and datasets; a narrow fastapi-only context omits the shared quality package.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build with the supplied root-context Dockerfile, run as UID 10001 and bind uvicorn to 0.0.0.0. Probe health/readiness and exercise every domain endpoint. Verify that the dataset path is readable under the non-root user and that credentials enter only at runtime.

For Qdrant server mode, restart the service with its named volume and repeat an authorized query. Read-only API filesystems require temporary/runtime artifacts to use explicitly permitted storage rather than the image layer.
sections.code:
docker compose up --build
# From another terminal, probe /health, /ready and /chat
# Confirm query 'retry HTTP 429' returns the authorized retry citation

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A Dockerfile copies ../datasets outside its build context and fails only in CI. A service imports the installed fastapi library instead of its app module. A relative data path silently loads no documents and produces abstention for every query.

Test a known retrieval question inside the container, not merely process startup. Check shutdown, port mapping and persistence. If Docker is unavailable in the development environment, record that execution limitation instead of claiming a smoke pass.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance evidence includes image identity, non-root identity, endpoint results, dataset path and restart behavior. Use the exact tested image for deployment and preserve its compatible rollback configuration.
For SDETs, environment tests should prove that a hand-computed fixture behaves the same inside and outside the container. This catches packaging defects independently of live model behavior.

mistake: A Dockerfile copies ../datasets outside its build context and fails only in CI. A service imports the installed fastapi library instead of its app module. A relative data path silently loads no documents and produces abstention for every query.
takeaway: Acceptance evidence includes image identity, non-root identity, endpoint results, dataset path and restart behavior.
